verifications.claim: The Iran nuclear agreement is officially known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) (R1); "Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action” (JCPOA) (R3); Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) (R4); Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly name the agreement as JCPOA.

verifications.claim: The JCPOA was reached on July 14, 2015.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact date confirmed in multiple references.

verifications.claim: The JCPOA was reached between Iran, the P5+1, and the European Union.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: P5+1 ... the European Union (EU), and Iran (R1); P5+1 ... European Union (EU) (R4); P5+1 ... European Union (R6); P5+1 ... European Union (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated parties match the claim.

verifications.claim: The P5+1 consists of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council—China, France, Russia, U.K., U.S.—plus Germany.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: P5+1 (China, France, Germany, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States) (R1); five permanent members ... (China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States) and Germany—collectively known as the P5+1 (R4); P5+1 (the five permanent members ... China, France, Russia, the U.K., U.S.—plus Germany) (R6)

verifications.claim: Breakout time is the time needed to produce enough weapons-grade uranium for a single nuclear weapon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: breakout time — the amount of time it would take to produce enough highly enriched fissile material for a nuclear weapon (R3); produce enough nuclear material for a weapon (R4); time ... enough 90%-enriched uranium to build a nuclear weapon - the so-called "break-out time" (R5)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, Iran agreed to constraints on its nuclear program to increase breakout time from two or three months to at least one year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: unwind Iran’s nuclear program to the point ... take at least one year ... in the absence of an agreement, Iran could produce enough nuclear material for a weapon in a few months (R4); two to three months ... increase its break-out time to one year or more (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Pre- and post-JCPOA breakout times exactly as stated.

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, Iran reduced its enriched uranium stockpile by 98%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: reduce its stockpile of uranium by 98% (R2); reduce its stockpile of low-enriched uranium by 97% (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states 98%; R6 says 97%, minor variance but clearly supported.

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, Iran capped enrichment levels at 3.67%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: keep its level of uranium enrichment at 3.67% (R2); limit enrichment to 3.67% (R4); limit enrichment to 3.67% (R6)

verifications.claim: 90% enrichment is required for weapons.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: enriching uranium-235 to 90% purity or higher (R3); High-enriched uranium, at some 90 percent, is used in nuclear weapons (R4)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, active centrifuges were reduced by two-thirds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: reduce its centrifuges to 6,104 ... nearly 20,000 centrifuges (R2 ~two-thirds); secure over two-thirds of its centrifuges in storage (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, active centrifuges were capped at 6,104 for ten years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: reduce its centrifuges to 6,104 for the next ten years (R2); reducing active units to 6,104 centrifuges ... for 10 years (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, only older models of centrifuges were allowed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: only centrifuges Iran will be allowed to use are their oldest and least efficient models (R2); limited to IR-1 centrifuges, Iran's oldest and least efficient (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, the Arak heavy-water reactor was redesigned to prevent it from producing weapons-grade plutonium.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Arak reactor will be redesigned so it cannot produce any weapons-grade plutonium (R2); modify Iran’s heavy water reactor at the Arak ... closed off the plutonium path (R3); modernize the Arak heavy water research reactor ... minimizing plutonium production (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, spent fuel from the Arak reactor was to be shipped out of the country.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: spent fuel rods (which could also be source material for weapons-grade plutonium) will be sent out of the country (R2); Spent fuel was to be sent out of the country (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, the IAEA was granted 24-hour surveillance of facilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: IAEA will have 24-hour access to nuclear facilities and maintain continuous monitoring (R2); IAEA was to have 24-hour access to nuclear facilities and maintain continuous monitoring (R6)

verifications.claim: Under the JCPOA, the IAEA was granted the ability to inspect suspicious sites.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: inspectors to access and inspect any site they deem suspicious (R2); allow inspectors ... unfettered access ... to undeclared sites (R4); allows inspectors to access any site anywhere ... they deem suspicious (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly grants inspection of suspicious sites.

verifications.claim: Implementation Day was January 16, 2016.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: January 16, 2016, marks Implementation Day (R1); implemented January 16, 2016 (R3); 16 January 2016 (implementation) (R6)

verifications.claim: The IAEA verified compliance by Iran on January 16, 2016.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: IAEA has verified that Iran has implemented its key nuclear-related measures ... January 16, 2016 (R1)

verifications.claim: Following IAEA verification on January 16, 2016, the U.S., EU, and UN lifted nuclear-related economic sanctions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: IAEA’s verification ... United States and the EU have lifted nuclear-related sanctions ... UN ... suspending their sanctions (R1, R3, R4)

verifications.claim: The lifting of nuclear-related economic sanctions allowed Iran to regain access to billions of dollars in frozen assets.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: unfroze about $100 billion worth of frozen Iranian assets (R4); gained access to more than $100bn in assets frozen overseas (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Billions in frozen assets explicitly mentioned.

verifications.claim: The lifting of nuclear-related economic sanctions allowed Iran to regain access to international oil markets.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: dropped secondary sanctions on the oil sector, which allowed Iran to ramp up its oil exports (R4); resume selling oil on international markets (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct access to oil markets post-sanctions lift.

verifications.claim: The JCPOA took effect on January 16, 2016.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: January 16, 2016, marks Implementation Day ... JCPOA came into effect (R1); JCPOA was implemented January 16, 2016 (R3); went into effect in January 2016 (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Implementation Day is when it took effect.

verifications.claim: President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from the JCPOA in May 2018.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: United States unilaterally withdrew ... 2018 (R3); withdrew the United States from it in 2018 (R4); May 2018 ... Donald Trump abandoned the JCPOA (R5); United States withdrew ... 2018 (R6)

verifications.claim: President Donald Trump called the JCPOA "defective at its core."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: calling it "defective at its core" (R5)

verifications.claim: President Donald Trump reinstated sanctions under a "maximum pressure" campaign.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: unilateral maximum pressure sanctions imposed by the United States (R3); "maximum pressure" campaign (R5)

verifications.claim: Following the U.S. withdrawal, Iran gradually stopped complying with the JCPOA restrictions in 2019.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: in 2019 Iran accelerated its uranium enrichment (R3); started exceeding agreed-upon limits ... in 2019 (R4); in 2019, Iran began breaching the deal's restrictions (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Timeline and gradual non-compliance post-withdrawal match.

verifications.claim: In 2019, Iran increased uranium enrichment to 60%.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: enriching uranium to 4.5% ... 5% (R6 2019); 60% purity ... By November 2021 (R5); 60 percent ... March 2025 (R3)
verifications.reasoning: 60% enrichment began in 2021, not 2019; 2019 increases were to lower levels.

verifications.claim: In 2019, Iran reduced IAEA access.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: increasingly limited the IAEA’s ability to inspect ... since Washington withdrew (R4); significantly curtailed access for international inspectors (R5 post-2018/2019 context)
verifications.reasoning: Reduction in access started post-2018 withdrawal, including 2019 breaches.

verifications.claim: President Joe Biden expressed a willingness to return to the JCPOA if Iran returned to full compliance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: President Joe Biden said that the United States would return to the JCPOA if Iran came back into compliance (R4)

verifications.claim: In April 2026, it was reported that Iran officially terminated the JCPOA after 10 years.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: 18 October 2025 ... termination of the agreement after 10 years (R6); expired on October 18, 2025 ... Iran announced ... no longer be bound (R8)
